chunks.transcript_text: If your ideas are too small, you need to think smaller. A lot of art directors and designers struggle with thinking conceptually because our visual brains jump straight to execution. Let's pull back and I'll show you how to think at different levels. This is the idea sizing chart. You can see that we have small ideas and big ideas. We're not talking about good ideas versus bad ideas. We're talking in terms of scale, literally large. We've got ideas that are smaller, tactics, which really don't even have an idea at all, one-offs, which are ideas that can only be one thing. We have executions, which could be any variety of expressions of a larger idea. And then we have campaigns and platforms, which are big ideas. They're larger, they're encompassing. Big ideas inspire other ideas. The big idea for the campaign is going to be expressed within the various executions of that campaign. A campaign idea that is so big that it could carry on for multiple years or be the idea that inspires multiple campaigns might be a platform. Now to think bigger you often need to think smaller You see the x is the level of detail You see that for executions you thinking through every detail What if we you know built a Nike shoe out of flowers and put it in Times Square? But you'll see big ideas don't have that level of detail. Big ideas should be inspired by a single insight articulated so concise that you can write it on a post-it note. Snickers has a famous idea, you're not you when you're hungry. It's a big idea because that's it. It articulates itself. There's no other level of detail needed. Nike had a campaign, winning isn't for everyone. You can also write it entirely on a post-it note and it's inspired by a single insight. The executions of those campaigns each express the big idea in a different way. For executions, you should be thinking through every detail, exactly how you're going to execute it, the look and feel, who, what, where. But before we get to this, a creative director or marketing team, they need to get to this. They need a guiding formula for the entire campaign. And that's how you think big. Ironically, you need something small and concise because they're high level ideas. And there's a whole lot more we could talk about, but I find that a lot of creatives just don't even know the size of ideas their creative director wants. Like, what exactly are we talking about here? This is one place to start. The idea sizes.
